title: Status Epilepticus
scenario: A 24-year-old male with a known seizure disorder is brought to the emergency department by paramedics after a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure that has continued for over 10 minutes without regaining consciousness.

lines: 24-year-old male brought in by EMS with ongoing generalized tonic-clonic seizure activity for >10 minutes per witness. Girlfriend reports he ran out of his levetiracetam 3 days ago. Continuous jerking of all four extremities, eyes deviated, frothing at the mouth. Unresponsive to voice. No IV access yet. Airway with copious oral secretions.

Side-lying position maintained, oral suction applied to clear secretions. High-flow O2 via non-rebreather placed. Bedrails padded and up. IV access being attempted. Fingerstick glucose obtained. Cardiac monitor and pulse oximetry applied.
IV lorazepam administered per order. Seizure activity slowed then stopped approximately 2 minutes after dose. Remains postictal and unresponsive to voice. IV levetiracetam loading dose infusing.
No further seizure activity for 45 minutes. Opens eyes to name, follows simple commands, oriented to person only. Breathing unlabored, secretions cleared. Moving all extremities.
Levetiracetam 1000 mg PO twice daily (home med, ran out 3 days ago)
Lorazepam 4 mg IV push now, may repeat once in 5 minutes if seizure continues
Levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV loading dose after benzodiazepine
Maintain airway, high-flow oxygen, suction as needed
Stat CBC, CMP, lactate, CK, antiepileptic drug levels
Notify provider for recurrent seizure activity

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which 4 findings on arrival require immediate follow-up?

options.text: Continuous seizure activity for more than 10 minutes
Copious oral secretions with no airway protection

children.rationale: Prolonged unremitting seizure activity, hypoxia, hypoventilation, and unprotected airway with secretions are life-threatening and demand immediate action. Low-grade fever and the diagnosis history are relevant but not the immediate threats.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it reflects a likely precipitant of the seizure, a physiologic consequence of prolonged seizing, or both.
children.rationale: Subtherapeutic drug levels and hyponatremia lower the seizure threshold and precipitate seizures. Elevated lactate, CK, and temperature result from sustained muscle activity during prolonged seizing.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse identifies that the priority need is {1}, and the first medication the nurse anticipates administering is {2}.

choices.text: maintaining a patent airway and oxygenation

children.rationale: Airway and oxygenation are the immediate priority in status epilepticus. A benzodiazepine such as lorazepam is the first-line agent to stop ongoing seizure activity before a longer-acting antiepileptic is loaded.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client during active seizure.

rows.text: Position the client on their side
Apply suction to clear oral secretions
Insert a padded oral airway by forcing the jaw open
Restrain the extremities to stop the movements

children.rationale: Side-lying positioning, suctioning, benzodiazepines, and oxygen protect the airway and stop seizures. Forcing objects into the mouth and restraining limbs cause injury and are contraindicated.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: After administering IV lorazepam, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Monitor respiratory rate and depth for depression
Continue to monitor SpO2 and blood pressure
Administer the ordered levetiracetam loading dose
Keep suction and airway equipment at the bedside
Ambulate the client to assess neurologic status

children.rationale: Lorazepam causes respiratory and CNS depression, so the nurse monitors ventilation, oxygenation, and blood pressure, keeps airway equipment ready, and gives the longer-acting antiepileptic. Ambulating a postictal client is unsafe and withholding therapy risks recurrence.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Follows simple commands and opens eyes to name

children.rationale: Cessation of seizures, improved oxygenation, recovering level of consciousness, and stable unlabored breathing show effective treatment. Continued jerking would indicate ongoing status epilepticus.
